claim: The new metadata guard returns for every closed generic type, not just generic value types. Closed generic classes from referenced assemblies previously reached the closed-generic GetObjectInfo path without crashing; they now exit before collection, removing their formatter from the consuming compilation's generated output. This changes the explicitly required 'closed generic classes keep working as before' behaviour and can leave the consuming resolver unable to supply the previously generated Item<int> formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the repro library with `public partial class Item<T>` and a valid [Key(0)] property, then compile the app with Cmd.Member of type Item<int> and run MessagePackGenerator on base and head. Compare the generated formatter/resolver sources: base contains the collected Lib.Item<int> formatter and registration, while this guard on head bypasses that collection. The regression test should require the head output to retain the same Item<int> formatter and resolver registration as base.

claim: The new property-location helper also returns null for source-declared positional record properties, whose declaration syntax is a ParameterSyntax rather than a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For `[MessagePackObject] partial record R([property: Key(null)] string Value)`, `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` is therefore created with `Location.None` and then discarded by `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, silently losing the analyzer error for an invalid key even though the property is in the current compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.PositionalRecordNullKeyDiagnosticReceiptTests.NullKeyOnPositionalRecordPropertyIsStillDiagnosed. It analyzes a source positional record with `[property: Key(null)]` and requires a diagnostic whose ID is `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull.Id`; on head the helper supplies no source location and the new reporting filter drops it.

claim: The unkeyed-member regression test does not exercise the metadata-safe MemberNeedsKey diagnostic change. The new early return skips every metadata-defined generic type before member collection, so restoring the original DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing would leave all three new tests passing.
